TOM DICKSON.name: Tom Dickson
TOM DICKSON.background: Republican from Cohutta (Whitfield County). Born Sept. 22, 1945, in Paradise, Pennsylvania; has lived in Whitfield County since 1967. Educator for 34 years, mostly with Whitfield County Schools; school system administrator 1976-1998 and Whitfield County schools superintendent 1998-2003. Education: bachelor's, Maryville College; master's in education, University of Tennessee at Chattanooga; educational specialist degree, State University of West Georgia. Methodist; married, two grown children. State Representative for House District 6 (parts of Whitfield, Murray and Catoosa counties), January 2005 to January 2017.
TOM DICKSON.ideology: Mainstream House Republican aligned with chamber leadership: Speaker David Ralston called him "probably the most solid guy in the Georgia House," and legislative leaders and the House Republican caucus PAC funded his 2016 re-election (AJC, May 2016). He lost the 2016 runoff to first-time candidate Jason Ridley, who said he ran because politicians don't listen to ordinary people.
TOM DICKSON.record: Served six terms in the Georgia House (2005-2017). Named chairman of the House Human Relations and Aging Committee by Speaker Ralston in April 2010 (after serving as vice chairman); later chaired the Appropriations subcommittee on education and sat on Education, Economic Development and Tourism, Regulated Industries, Rules and Reapportionment. Appeared in the 2011 documentary "Bully" after the suicide of a 17-year-old constituent, Tyler Long. In the May 24, 2016 Republican primary he led with 2,766 votes (49.7%), falling 16 votes short of an outright win over Jason Ridley (32.1%) and Sarah Fields (18.2%); he lost the July 26 runoff to Ridley, 1,564 (46.0%) to 1,839 (54.0%), ending a 12-year legislative career.
TOM DICKSON.notes: Former incumbent (HD 6, 2005-2017). "Tom" Dickson and shows scorecards (AFP-Georgia, Georgia Chamber, NFIB, ACU 2012-2016) but no Dickson scores, so no ratings entered. State roll-call votes and bills omitted per instructions (available from General Assembly records). Positions are from his 2010 race; no 2016 issue statements were found. GeorgiaPol (political blog, May 2016) described him as a target of 'purity now!' forces in northwest Georgia; not used for labels. House-press 2010 release gives both 2004 (elected) and 2005 (took office).

positions.stance: Called the state budget "the big issue"; expected needs to exceed available resources after recession cuts.
Supported expanding the 287(g) program giving local agencies access to ICE databases; opposed a state mandate but favored helping cover costs or offering incentives.

Favored incentives for businesses to expand and create jobs, saying government cannot create jobs; backed bills giving tax breaks to employers that hire unemployed people (vetoed twice by Gov. Sonny Perdue).

statements.text: After losing the runoff: "Obviously, I'm disappointed with the results. But I'll be OK."
On illegal immigration enforcement gaps: "That makes no sense to me"; on the unemployed: "We need to do what we can to help them."

VALERIE CLARK.name: Valerie Clark
VALERIE CLARK.background: Republican from Gwinnett County (38 years in the same Lawrenceville-area home as of 2016). Retired educator: Gwinnett teacher and principal of Duluth Middle, Shiloh Middle and Central Gwinnett High. SUNY Plattsburgh; M.Ed., UNC Chapel Hill; Ph.D., University of Georgia. Married to Dr. Bob Clark, retired school administrator and former Lawrenceville city councilman; two children.
